messages.content: You are a meticulous energy-infrastructure research agent. Your task is to produce a comprehensive, source-grounded inventory of Vietnam thermal power generation assets over 30 MWe. Use web retrieval aggressively but budget-consciously. Never fabricate a source, URL, plant, date, capacity, owner, or status. Separate discovery sources from admissible justification sources. Prefer Vietnamese official sources, PDP documents, EVN/PVN/PV Power/Vinacomin/PetroVietnam/GENCO/BOT/operator disclosures, MOIT/ERAV/NSMO/NLDC/regulator documents, provincial documents, EIA documents, annual reports, exchange filings, and multilateral reports. Tertiary compilations may only be used for leads and must not be cited as support in final claims. Always preserve uncertainty explicitly. Use calibrated confidence: HIGH only with at least two independent concordant sources with at least one primary; MEDIUM for one primary or sourced aggregator with verifiable primary; LOW for secondary-only, inferred, unresolved, or source-not-found rows. Apply freshness ceilings to status claims. If evidence conflicts, reconcile explicitly, choose the higher-tier or fresher source as appropriate, and record the conflict. The final report must be a single Markdown document with sector overview, structured table, summaries, narratives, and annotated bibliography. Keep generation concise enough to remain within budget; prioritize recall, provenance, and uncertainty over prose polish.

Produce a complete, primary-sourced reference inventory of Vietnam's past, present, and future thermal generation assets above 30 MWe, including coal, domestic gas, and imported LNG. Include grid-connected, micro-grid, off-grid, captive, CHP, industrial, operating, retired, under construction, approved, planned, suspended, cancelled, and pre-FID projects if they appeared in formal planning cycles. Work in phases under the session budget. Do not produce the final report on the first turn unless you already have sufficient sourced evidence. Use up to three planning/search turns, then a final Markdown report, then one verify-and-polish pass if offered. RESEARCH STRATEGY 1. Start with official planning and system-wide sources to build the universe of assets: Vietnam Power Development Plans VI/VII/revised VII/VIII and PDP8 implementation plan; MOIT/ERAV/EVN annual reports; NSMO/NLDC generation lists if available; Vietnam Energy Outlook; JICA/World Bank/ADB documents; operator annual reports. 2. Then search by asset groups and institutions: EVN, GENCO1/2/3, PVN/PV Power, Vinacomin/TKV, AES, BOT project companies, provincial people’s committees, EIA approvals, EPC/financing disclosures. 3. Use Vietnamese search terms as well as English. Examples: “nhà máy nhiệt điện”, “trung tâm điện lực”, “tuabin khí”, “điện khí LNG”, “Quy hoạch điện VIII”, “Quyết định phê duyệt”, “báo cáo thường niên”, plus plant names. 4. Use tertiary trackers or encyclopedias only as discovery checklists. If a lead is found there, trace to an admissible source. If no admissible source is found, include the asset if plausibly in scope, set Source = “not found”, Confidence = LOW, and mention the inadmissible lead only in Notes. 5. For each plant, try to obtain two independent sources, ideally at least one official or operator primary source. Independence means different evidentiary origins, not merely different webpages repeating the same release. SOURCE HIERARCHY FOR FINAL JUSTIFICATION Admissible primary sources: official government documents; regulator-aggregated official data; operator filings, annual reports, investor presentations, stock-exchange disclosures, official press releases, environmental/permit documents, official project-company documents. Admissible secondary sources: international-institution reports; bylined trade press; reputable industry trackers/data brokers only where they expose the primary source supporting the value. Not admissible for final support: Wikipedia/Wikidata/DBpedia, mirrors, unsourced aggregators, SEO pages, data deposits without per-value provenance, and re-syndicated content without independent verification. ROW AND STATUS RULES - Row unit: plant/unit-group by default. Split co-located assets when capacity, COD, owner/developer, fuel, status, technology, or financing/project arrangements differ. Aggregate only if detailed evidence is unavailable; mark ambiguous in Notes. - Include only assets >30 MWe. Use nameplate electrical MWe where available. If gross/net is unclear, keep stated MW and note “gross/net unspecified”. Do not use thermal MW, boiler t/h, steam output, or investment package capacity as electrical capacity. - Status vocabulary only: Operational, Under construction, Approved, Planned, Suspended, Cancelled, Retired. - Status as-of-date: best date on which status was attested or became effective. Also account for publication freshness in confidence. - COD: use year or exact date if available; for multi-unit plants use range or unit years. For planned assets use expected COD only if clearly stated; otherwise “not found”. CONFIDENCE RULES - HIGH = at least two independent concordant admissible sources, at least one primary. - MEDIUM = one primary source, or sourced aggregator/secondary citing a verifiable primary. - LOW = secondary only, inferred, unresolved conflict, stale evidence, or source not found. Hard ceilings: - Commercial operator self-report not confirmed by official source: cap at MEDIUM. - Status attested only by a source older than 24 months and unconfirmed since: cap status at MEDIUM; if older than 48 months, cap status at LOW. - Source = not found rows are LOW. Expose row-level existence/status confidence in the main table. In plant narratives or Notes, qualify disputed capacity, status, fuel, COD, owner/operator, or location where needed using: value — level — evidence/agreement basis — sources. FINAL REPORT FORMAT: SINGLE MARKDOWN DOCUMENT Use this structure: 1. Title, date of compilation, scope statement, confidence methodology, and caveats. 2. Sector overview: electricity mix, policy framework, key institutional actors, current challenges. Keep concise and cite sources. 3. Inventory method and source hierarchy. 4. Structured power-plants table with exactly these columns: Name (Vietnamese) | Name (English) | Province | Fuel (Coal / Domestic gas / Imported LNG) | Technology (Subcritical / Supercritical / USC for coal; CCGT / OCGT for gas) | Units × MW | Total MWe | Status | Status as-of-date | COD | Owner/Developer | Confidence | Source 1 | Source 2 | Notes 5. Concise sourced per-plant narratives. Prioritize major, disputed, ambiguous, cancelled, under-construction, LNG, BOT, captive/CHP, and historically important assets. For straightforward assets, keep narrative to one or two sentences or rely on Notes if budget is tight. 6. Statistical summary tables: a. Capacity by fuel × status. b. Top 15 provinces by capacity. c. Timeline of additions by period and fuel, separating actual COD from expected COD. d. Data-quality summary by confidence level and fuel. Ensure totals reconcile with the structured table; state if cancelled/planned capacity is included separately. 7. Annotated bibliography of every cited source. For each source include full citation, URL when available, original-language title and English translation for non-English sources, publication date or access/as-of date, type/tier, and a short annotation describing exactly what was drawn from it. BUDGET DISCIPLINE - Preserve recall, provenance, and uncertainty notes over long prose. - Do not over-cite every cell if it would blow the budget; instead cite row-level sources that support the key row attributes, and call out unsupported/disputed cells in Notes. - If the source universe is too large, produce the best comprehensive table first, then shorter narratives and bibliography annotations. - If budget becomes tight, stop searching and produce the final report with clear gaps. STOPPING CRITERIA BEFORE FINAL REPORT Proceed to the final report when you have: (1) a reasonably complete asset universe from planning/system sources plus tracker cross-checking; (2) at least one admissible source for most operational/major planned assets; (3) uncertainty flags for remaining leads; and (4) enough data to compute summary tables. Do not omit known plants just because sourcing is weak; include with LOW confidence and explain. # Evidence pack These are manually curated primary sources meant to boost but not replace your own deep research. 1. evn_ar_2010_2011_capacities — EVN Annual Report 2010-2011 2. evn_ar_2017_capacities — Vietnam Electricity Annual Report 2017 3. evn_ar_2018_capacities — Vietnam Electricity Annual Report 2018 4. pdp7a_annex1_table1 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 5. pdp7a_annex1_table2 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 6. pdp7a_annex1_table3 — Revised PDP7 Annex I 7. pdp7_annex1 — PDP7 Annex I 8. pdp7_annex2 — PDP7 Annex II 9. pdp8_annex2_table1 — PDP8 Annex II 10. pdp8_annex2_table2 — PDP8 Annex II 11. pdp8_annex2_table3 — PDP8 Annex II 12. pdp8_annex2_table4 — PDP8 Annex II 13. pdp8_annex2_table5 — PDP8 Annex II 14. report_32_annex1 — Report 32 Annex 1 15. report_58_annex — Report 58 Annex 16. study_e542_pl9_1 — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex 17. study_e542_pl9_2 — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex 18. study_e542_pl9_5a — PDP8 draft 3 study E-542 annex ## Chunk 1 source_id: evn_ar_2010_2011_capacities file: EVN_Annual_Report_2010_2011_CapacitiesTable.md document_title: EVN Annual Report 2010-2011 section_title: Corporate overview - installed capacity of power plants as of 31/12/2011 source_type: operator annual report table extract relevance: Installed-capacity and owner baseline from EVN for the 2011 system, including thermal plants alongside other generation types <<>> # EVN Annual Report 2010-2011, pp 13-14 ## Corporate overview ### Công suất đặt các nhà máy điện tính tới 31/12/2011

Includes grid-connected, captive/industrial/CHP, BOT, IPP, state-owned, operating, retired, under construction, approved, planned, suspended, and cancelled/superseded projects where found in formal planning documents.  
**Main limitation:** This is a best-effort reference inventory prepared under the session budget. The table emphasizes **recall and provenance** over perfect plant-level engineering detail. ## 1. Confidence methodology and caveats

**Confidence levels**

- **HIGH** — at least two independent concordant admissible sources, at least one primary or official/operator source.
- **MEDIUM** — one primary/official/operator source, or a credible secondary/institutional source tied to a verifiable primary.
- **LOW** — old planning-only source, secondary-only source, stale status evidence, unresolved conflict, or “not found” for a second admissible source.

**Hard ceilings applied**

- If status is attested only by stale planning material older than 48 months, status confidence is capped at LOW.
- If a project appears in PDP7/PDP7A but not PDP8/PDP8 implementation materials and no later project evidence was found, it is usually classified **Cancelled** or **Suspended** with LOW confidence.
- Where nameplate differs by source, the table uses the most recent project/operator/planning figure, with older conflicting values noted.

**Administrative geography caveat**

Vietnam’s 2025 provincial reorganization affects several locations. Where current official pages use new province names — e.g., Quảng Trạch I now described by EVN as in **Quảng Trị province**, formerly Quảng Bình — the table generally records the current province and notes the historical province where relevant. EVN’s 2026 Quảng Trạch I updates identify the project in Phú Trạch commune, Quảng Trị province, formerly Quảng Đông commune, Quảng Trạch district, Quảng Bình province. ([vietnaminsiders.com](https://vietnaminsiders.com/unit-1-of-vietnam-duyen-hai-ii-thermal-power-project-2x660mw-was-officially-put-into-commercial-operation/?utm_source=openai))

## 2. Sector overview

Vietnam’s power system reached about **82,387 MW installed capacity in 2024**, of which EVN’s annual-report data show **coal-fired capacity at 26,757 MW** and **gas + oil-fired capacity at 8,653 MW**. This system baseline is useful for reconciling plant-level thermal capacity, though it does not itself provide full plant-level detail. ([genco3.com](https://www.genco3.com/data/files/20240819/638596636042140173_0.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The main policy framework is built from PDP7, Revised PDP7, PDP8, and the PDP8 Implementation Plan. PDP8 was approved by Decision 500/QĐ-TTg on 15 May 2023, while the PDP8 Implementation Plan was approved by Decision 262/QĐ-TTg on 1 April 2024. Legal summaries and the official English-hosted Decision 262 file indicate that the implementation plan translates PDP8 into investment/action lists and project status information. ([genco3.com](https://www.genco3.com/data/files/20250418/638805915383074592_0.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Key institutional actors include **EVN**, EVN’s generation corporations **GENCO1/GENCO2/GENCO3**, **PVN/PV Power**, **Vinacomin/TKV**, BOT project companies, foreign sponsors such as AES, Sumitomo, Marubeni/KEPCO, Janakuasa, VAPCO, and provincial/industrial developers. EVN’s current public information also shows continued emphasis on fuel supply coordination with Vinacomin, Dong Bac, PVN, and PVGas. ([bctn.genco3.com](https://bctn.genco3.com/en/general-information-about-evngenco3/?utm_source=openai))

Current challenges include delayed coal BOTs, coal-to-LNG conversion pressure, domestic-gas field synchronization problems, LNG fuel/PPA bankability, and the need to maintain thermal availability during high-demand periods. EVN reported that coal-fired thermal plants accounted for the largest share of installed capacity at end-2023, while gas power output was constrained by domestic gas supply in 2024. ([genco3.com](https://www.genco3.com/en-us.html?utm_source=openai))

Vietnam’s older coal fleet consists largely of northern mine-mouth or domestic-coal plants: Uông Bí, Phả Lại, Ninh Bình, Hải Phòng, Quảng Ninh, Na Dương, Cao Ngạn, Cẩm Phả, Sơn Động, Mạo Khê, An Khánh, and Thăng Long. EVN annual reports for 2011, 2017, and 2018 provide a reliable operator-side baseline for EVN/GENCO assets, while PDP7/PDP7A provide commissioning-lineage evidence. The oldest retirements are clearest for Uông Bí old 105 MW and planned Ninh Bình/Uông Bí/Cần Thơ retirements in PDP7/PDP7A, but fresh retirement confirmations were not all found within the budget.

### Coal fleet — major post-2010 additions

Major operating additions include Vũng Áng I, Mông Dương I/II, Vĩnh Tân I/II/IV, Duyên Hải I/II/III/III Extension, Hải Dương BOT, Nghi Sơn II, Vân Phong I, Sông Hậu I, Vũng Áng II, and Quảng Trạch I. Vân Phong I is confirmed as 1,320 MW, ultra-supercritical, inaugurated in March 2024, and in operation after completion around January 2024. ([vietnamnews.vn](https://vietnamnews.vn/economy/1651894/van-phong-1-bot-thermal-power-plant-becomes-operational.html?utm_source=openai))

Vũng Áng II is now effectively operational: VAPCO’s official company overview identifies the project as a **2×665 MW ultra-supercritical imported-coal BOT plant**, with Unit 1 in commercial operation from **22 July 2025**; SGGP reported Unit 2 entered commercial operations at midnight on **7 April 2026**, bringing the project to full operation. ([vapco.vn](https://vapco.vn/en/gioi-thieu-cong-ty/overview/?utm_source=openai))

Quảng Trạch I remains in the construction/commissioning transition as of this compilation. EVN reports it is a **2×701.5 MW / 1,403 MW USC** coal plant; Unit 1 synchronized to the grid on **12 April 2026** and completed first coal firing on **6 May 2026**, but a COD confirmation was not found before finalization. ([pecc2ese.com](https://pecc2ese.com/en/duyen-hai-2-thermal-power-plant?utm_source=openai))

### Suspended/delayed coal projects

PDP8 Table 3 explicitly identifies delayed coal projects with financing/shareholder difficulties: **Cẩm Thanh/Công Thanh, Nam Định I, Quảng Trị, Vĩnh Tân III, and Sông Hậu II**. Công Thanh/Cẩm Thanh is especially uncertain because PDP8 states that MOIT should work with investors and consider termination if it could not be implemented by June 2024. These rows remain MEDIUM or LOW pending updated MOIT/provincial termination evidence.

### Cancelled/superseded coal option space

Many PDP7/PDP7A long-horizon coal projects did not survive into PDP8 as coal projects, including Kiên Lương, Hải Phòng III, Quảng Ninh III, Vũng Áng III, Bạc Liêu coal, Bình Định coal, An Giang coal, and generic northern/southern coal blocks. E542 and PDP8 show a broad migration from coal option space to LNG option space, especially for Long An, Bạc Liêu, Quảng Ninh, Quảng Trạch II, Quỳnh Lập/Nghi Sơn, and Tân Phước.

### Domestic gas fleet

The established domestic-gas fleet is concentrated in the southeast and southwest: Phú Mỹ I/II.1/II.2/III/IV, Bà Rịa, Nhơn Trạch I/II, Cà Mau I/II, and Ô Môn I. PDP8 adds or reaffirms new Lô B / Cá Voi Xanh / Báo Vàng-linked domestic gas projects: Ô Môn II/III/IV, Dung Quất I/II/III, Miền Trung I/II, and Quảng Trị CCGT. The principal uncertainty is synchronization with upstream gas development.

Phú Mỹ III’s status changed institutionally: EVN reported that it took over Phú Mỹ 3 from **1 March 2024** and was negotiating gas supply with PVN/PVGAS. ([en.evn.com.vn](https://en.evn.com.vn/d6/news/Uong-Bi-Thermal-Power-drastically-implements-solutions-to-improve-the-reliability-and-availability-of-generating-units-66-163-4005.aspx?utm_source=openai))

### LNG projects

PDP8’s LNG list is the current-policy backbone. It includes Quảng Ninh, Thái Bình, Nghi Sơn, Quảng Trạch II, Quỳnh Lập/Nghi Sơn, Hải Lăng phase 1, Cà Ná, Sơn Mỹ I/II, Long Sơn, Nhơn Trạch 3&4, Hiệp Phước, Long An I/II, and Bạc Liêu.

Nhơn Trạch 3&4 is the most advanced LNG project found in this pass. PV Power reported the PPA signing and project reverse energization, and PV Power’s May 2024 update said construction progress was about **85%**. ([pvpower.vn](https://pvpower.vn/en/post/power-purchase-agreement-for-nhon-trach-3-4-power-plant-6170.htm?utm_source=openai))

### Captive / industrial / CHP

The largest formal industrial/captive group is Formosa Hà Tĩnh, including coal-fired and blast-furnace-gas units, later summarized in PDP8 as **Formosa HT2 650 MW** in the cogeneration/waste-heat/by-product category. Hải Hà CHP 1–4, Đức Giang CHP, Hòa Phát II residual-gas power, and Long Sơn petrochemical CHP appear in PDP8/PDP7A planning cycles. These rows are included to preserve recall but carry lower confidence where plant-level operator evidence was not found.
